character: vain mink, sleek glossy dark-brown fur, in a rich sheepskin coat embroidered with red, blue and yellow patterns and a tall black fur papakha, smug, always in motion
props: picket fence across a snowy yard, intact all clip; smoking grill with shashlik beyond; metal skewers; red rag; five scruffy half-rats at the pickets close to the lens — scrawny father, fat mother, three kids, patchy dull fur
motion_rule: mink crosses to a new spot every window, never speaks from one place; shot size changes every window; the rats do a new gag every window, large and close to the lens
environment: snowy backyard, bright sunny midday, hard shadows

audio.delivery: smug female voice, native Russian stress, calm
audio.pronunciation: stress: shi-KAR-ny, se-BYA, GLAV-no-ye, sa-SYE-di, za-VEE-do-va-li — never ZA-vi-do-va-li
audio.pacing: brisk lively pacing, no drawling, lines fit the windows
audio.lip_sync: mouth opens and closes clearly on every syllable, never a voice-over

timeline.a: mink bursts from a snowbank in a blast of snow, coat flaring | all five rats at the grill snap their heads round
mink flings the coat open, dark fur blazing with shifting highlights at the lens | fat mother drops her shashlik, jaw hanging
mink struts left along the fence, coat hem sweeping snow, papakha tilting | three kids scramble up the pickets in a stack, teeth clacking
mink spins hard, coat flying out in a full circle, fur fanning | father vaults the grill, the whole family slams into the pickets, five faces filling the foreground
mink shakes snow off in a wide fan | father thrusts both paws across the pickets begging, she flips him the skewers
mink glides along the pickets right to left, fur brushing the tops | mother gnaws a picket, kids hanging off her tail, smoke pouring from the grill
mink leaps a snowbank, coat and fur fanning mid-air | the family lunges, kids catch her tail in their teeth and are dragged through the snow
mother jabs a skewer into her own left eye, paw on it, aims the other at the mink | mink dashes past, flicking snow at them
mother ties the red rag on that eye like a pirate patch | father counts the mink's two eyes on his claws
all three kids copy her and raise skewers to their own eyes, father knocks them away | mink skids low through the snow to the fence
mother misjudges with one eye and headbutts the grill, shashlik raining on the kids | mink bounds a snowbank, lands spinning, papakha dropping onto her head
kids still locked on her tail by their teeth, dragged along the fence | mink races to the lens, snow spraying
mink sweeps to the pickets and swings her flared fur and coat across the lens | all five rats in a heap beyond, mother one-eyed under the red patch, beaming with envy

must_appear: fence intact every frame; her bare fur close and glinting at 0.3-1.55; five rats at the pickets, new gag every window; skewers given at 3.3; kids on her tail at 5.05 and 8.7; mother jabs her own eye at 6.3, rag as a patch to the end
negative_prompt: night, dark scene, dusk, evening, subtitles, captions, watermark, static camera, locked-off shots, same shot size twice, only her head moving, speaking from one spot, a window where the rats do nothing, the fence breaking, blood, extra limbs, character changing mid-shot, English speech, Latin letters, any word after 6.3
